LESSON: MANAGEMENT OF SOLID WASTE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Matter
Topic 2.2: Management of solid waste
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Management of solid waste, part of Matter in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: How is solid waste dangerous to the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Management of solid waste together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner reflects on ways of managing different types of waste in their

14

environment.

● Creativity and imagination: The learner explores ways of making dustbins for safe disposal of waste at home and in school

using locally available materials.

Values:
Responsibility: The learner uses proper safety measures in solid waste management. (wearing protective gears and use of

appropriate tools)

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Health Promotion Issues (preventive health): The learner discusses the dangers of solid waste to the environment and

presents in class.

• Socio-economic Issues (environmental education): The learner discusses ways of managing different types of solid waste in

their environment.

Link to other Learning area:

Creative arts: The learner uses knowledge on management of solid waste to make ornaments and dustbins.

Suggested Learning Resources

Solid wastes such as papers, plastics, glasses and food waste,

Braille materials and equipment,

Digital devices with assistive technology such as adapted keyboards, screen readers and screen magnifiers,

Print materials in appropriate font and colour contrast.
